conclusion_verdicts.question: On engine 1.2.0, does collection-level bulk_write work, ordered and unordered, and how is a duplicate _id reported?
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Rerun on t_bulk_rerun: ordered dup nInserted=2 with writeError index 2 code 11000; unordered nInserted=3 nMatched=1 nRemoved=1; states identical to the tester's; raw insert replies ok=1 with writeErrors in the body; write-error keys ['code', 'errmsg', 'index', 'op'] (PyMongo) and ['code', 'errmsg', 'index'] (server). 'Identical to 0.117' re-checked on this rerun: 20 of 20 common steps have the 0.117 signature.

conclusion_verdicts.question: How does the driver send a collection-level bulk_write to this engine?
conclusion_verdicts.verdict: confirmed; the hedge about regrouping is now resolved
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Wire capture reproduced exactly (1a [('insert', 2), ('update', 2), ('delete', 1)], 2a [('insert', 4)], 3a [('insert', 4), ('update', 1), ('delete', 1)]). Extra probe X3 with interleaved types: ordered -> [('insert', 1), ('update', 1), ('insert', 1), ('delete', 1), ('insert', 1), ('update', 1)] (one command per consecutive run), unordered -> [('insert', 3), ('update', 2), ('delete', 1)] (PyMongo 4.20.1 regroups all ops of a type into one command). This is driver behaviour; only PyMongo was exercised.

conclusion_verdicts.question: Does client-level MongoClient.bulk_write (the MongoDB 8.0 bulkWrite command) work on engine 1.2.0, and what does the raw bulkWrite command return?

Control X1a: an invented name returns code 59 CommandNotFound "Command 'noSuchCommandXyz' not found.", the same template as "Command 'bulkWrite' not found.". Gateway source at 965b6e7a (S5): from_str has no bulkWrite arm (case-insensitive 'bulk' occurrences: 0) and its default arm returns CommandNotFound "Command '{cmd_name}' not found."; the engine stub (S6) answers CommandNotSupported and is never reached.

disputed.question: What does hello.maxWriteBatchSize advertise on the 1.2.0 gateway (DECISIONS topic 9, open item 4)?
disputed.reason: The answer says the 25,000 observation 'settles open item 4 for documentdb-local 1.2.0 only'. Open item 4 in DECISIONS topic 9 asks only what the Azure gateway advertises, so a documentdb-local run settles none of it and the item must stay open. What the run does settle is the open-source half, and the gateway source at the image revision (S1-S4) shows why: 100,000 is only the fallback when the engine GUC documentdb.maxWriteBatchSize is absent, so the DECISIONS settled-item phrase 'the advertised driver split size defaults to 100,000' is wrong for this code. For Azure the question becomes what documentdb.maxWriteBatchSize is set to there, which is still unobserved.

disputed.question: Did anything in bulk-write behaviour change between engine 0.117 and 1.2.0?
disputed.reason: Two generalizations go beyond the evidence, which comes from PyMongo 4.20.1 only. (1) 'so drivers still gate MongoClient.bulk_write off': PyMongo refuses it client-side (wire 21 < 25), but no other driver was run; a driver that does send the command gets 59 CommandNotFound instead. (2) '5 of 5 ENGINE-TESTS.md bulk-write claims hold' counts claim 2 ('as every driver does') and claim 4 ('drivers split larger batches automatically') as holding, although only PyMongo was observed. Those claims should say 'PyMongo'. Separately, 3 of the '20 common steps' (0c-pymongo, 6c-drop-big2, 7-dropDatabase) do not test the engine. The core finding, no bulk-write behaviour change from 0.117 to 1.2.0, stands.

extra_observations: Source-level confirmation at the image's OCI revision 965b6e7a (S1-S4, S7): the gateway's hello and isMaster reply take maxWriteBatchSize from the engine GUC documentdb.maxWriteBatchSize, read through pg_settings with the 'documentdb.' prefix stripped. The advertised split size and the enforced cap are the same engine variable (MaxWriteBatchSize, default 25,000), so they cannot drift apart unless the GUC is missing (then the gateway falls back to 100,000) or is overridden for some sessions only (it is PGC_USERSET; no such override was observed). The host config file cannot set the value: this revision copies only IsPrimary and SendShutdownResponses from it.

bulkWrite is answered exactly like a command name that does not exist. An invented name returns 59 CommandNotFound "Command 'noSuchCommandXyz' not found." (X1a), and the gateway's command table at 965b6e7a has no bulkWrite entry (S5). The engine's CommandNotSupported stub ('bulkWrite is not yet implemented', S6) is never reached. 'Not recognised by the gateway (59 CommandNotFound)' is the accurate wording. The 'Engine tests' headline in DECISIONS.md says 'client-level bulkWrite is unsupported (code 59)', which reads as 115 CommandNotSupported; code 59 is CommandNotFound.

PyMongo 4.20.1 regroups unordered batches. Interleaved insert/update/insert/delete/insert/update goes out as [('insert', 3), ('update', 2), ('delete', 1)] when unordered and as [('insert', 1), ('update', 1), ('insert', 1), ('delete', 1), ('insert', 1), ('update', 1)] when ordered (X3). An unordered batch therefore runs in type order, not in the order given. This is driver behaviour, and the engine accepts both forms.

Driver splitting at hello.maxWriteBatchSize also covers update and delete batches: 25,001 UpdateOne -> [('update', 25000), ('update', 1)] (all 25001 updated), 25,001 DeleteOne -> [('delete', 25000), ('delete', 1)] (count after: 0) (X4). The tester showed this for inserts only.
The legacy isMaster command that drivers use for the initial handshake advertises the same limits as hello: maxWriteBatchSize 25000, maxWireVersion 21, msg 'isdbgrid' (X2).

Duplicate-key write errors carry only index, code and errmsg, and the errmsg is a fixed template naming only the index: ["Duplicate key violation on the requested collection: Index '_id_'", "Duplicate key violation on the requested collection: Index 'email_1'"] for _id and for a secondary unique index (steps 2a, 4, X5b, X5c). There is no keyPattern, no keyValue, no namespace, no duplicated value, and no 'E11000' prefix. Code that parses MongoDB's 'E11000 duplicate key error ...' text or reads keyValue to find the duplicated field gets nothing. Match on code 11000 and, if needed, on the index name. The Azure run 02-real-time-event-stream-ingestion/20261124-203233 logged the same template ("Duplicate key violation on the requested collection: Index 'customer_event_unique'"), which is consistent with, not proof of, the same engine lineage on the managed service.

The batch cap is checked on the operation count before anything is written. In source the checks sit in the spec-building step (BuildBatchInsertionSpec, PostProcessDeleteBatchSpec, BuildUpdates) or at the start of the update batch worker (S8a-S8c). On the wire, the rejected 25,001-document insert came back in 2.2 ms; the accepted 25,000-document insert command in 6a took 55.5 ms. update with 0 statements is also code 16 per source (S8c); only insert with 0 documents was exercised.

Reproduction was exact. All 40 steps of run.py plus the read-only checks (35 wire steps and 8a-8e) have the same command, response, wire capture and reading as the tester's report after normalising the database name and dropping timings, localTime and connectionId. Differences: none.
notes: Only database t_bulk_rerun was used. It did not exist before the run (preflight.json), was dropped at the start and end of run.py and of extra_probes.py, and was confirmed absent afterwards (7b, X9b). The container was neither stopped nor modified; 8a-8e are read-only (docker inspect, grep over two binaries, key names of the gateway config files, one SELECT on pg_settings). The source files came from public raw.githubusercontent.com URLs at the image revision; they were read as text and never executed. Rerun with run_all.sh.
